info.name: Scarlata API (v1)
info.description:
Scarlata - Costa Rica outdoor-spot tracker. Local dev API.

WHAT THIS API IS SHAPED LIKE
- Auth is SESSION COOKIES, not tokens. There is no Authorization header anywhere in this API.
  Run 'Auth > 2. Login' once and Postman carries the cookie automatically for localhost:3001.
  If requests suddenly start returning 401, the session expired (24h) - just log in again.
- Every request that sends a body sends JSON, with Content-Type: application/json.
- Reads are public. Writes to /spots are ADMIN ONLY - users do not create spots.

VARIABLES
- baseUrl   comes from the 'Scarlata - Local' environment
- spotId    filled in for you by 'List all spots' and 'Create spot', so you should never need
            to paste an id by hand

SUGGESTED FIRST RUN
  1. Auth > 1. Register                 you are now a normal user
  2. Spots - public > List all spots
  3. Error cases > 403                  proves users cannot create spots
  4. Promote yourself to admin          see the 'Create spot' description, then Login again
  5. Spots - admin only > Create spot

Only endpoints that EXIST TODAY are in here. toVisit/visited, votes, reviews, visit logs and the
progress endpoints are Parts 3-7 in TODO.md, and get added to this collection as they land.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Register / login / logout. Start here - almost everything else needs a session.

request.description:
Creates an account and signs you in immediately - the response sets the session cookie,
so you do not need to call Login right after.

BODY: username, email, password. All three required.

NEW ACCOUNTS ARE ALWAYS role='user'. There is deliberately no route that grants admin.
See 'Spots - admin only > Create spot' for how to promote yourself.

Success: 201 Created
Errors:  409 if the email or username is already taken
         400 if the password is missing

exec: pm.test("no password hash leaks in the response", () => {

request.description:
Signs in and sets the session cookie. Postman stores cookies per domain automatically, so
every request after this one is authenticated - you do not add any header yourself.

BODY: username + password.
NOTE: the 'username' field also accepts the EMAIL address. The User model passes
usernameQueryFields: ['email'] to passport-local-mongoose, so login matches on either one.

Success: 200 OK
Errors:  401 on wrong credentials

exec: console.log('Signed in as', u.username, '| role:', u.role);

request.description:
Returns the signed-in user. The React client will call this on page load to work out
whether it has a session at all.

NO BODY. Requires the session cookie.

Success: 200 OK
Errors:  401 if signed out

exec: console.log('Signed in as', u.username, '| role:', u.role);

request.description:
Destroys the session.

NO BODY, no headers.

Success: 200 OK

NO BODY, NO AUTH.

item.name: Spots - admin only
item.description: Curation. Every request here needs role='admin' - see 'Create spot' for how to get it.

body.raw:
{
  "name": "Catarata del Toro",
  "description": "A 90m waterfall dropping into an extinct volcanic crater near Bajos del Toro.",
  "province": "Alajuela",
  "activityTypes": ["waterfall", "hiking"],
  "difficulty": "moderate",
  "bestTimeOfDay": "morning",
  "waterfallHeightM": 90,
  "trailLengthKm": 1.5,
  "estimatedDurationHrs": 2,
  "swimmable": false,
  "oneDayTrip": true,
  "location": {
    "type": "Point",
    "coordinates": [-84.2247, 10.2081]
  }
}

request.description:
Adds a spot to the map. ADMIN ONLY.

HOW TO BECOME AN ADMIN - there is no route for it, on purpose. Register normally, then flip
the field directly in MongoDB:

    mongosh scarlata
    db.users.updateOne({ username: 'samuel' }, { $set: { role: 'admin' } })

Then run 'Auth > 2. Login' again so the session picks up the new role.

BODY - required: name, province, difficulty, location.coordinates

  province       one of the seven, spelled WITH ACCENTS exactly as in models/spot.js:
                 San Jose / Alajuela / Cartago / Heredia / Guanacaste / Puntarenas / Limon
                 (copy the accented spellings out of the model - the enum is strict)
  difficulty     easy | moderate | hard
  activityTypes  array. hiking, waterfall, river, camping, viewpoint, hot-springs,
                 hanging-bridges, zipline, rafting, snorkeling
  coordinates    [longitude, latitude] - LONGITUDE FIRST. That is GeoJSON order and it is the
                 reverse of what Google Maps shows you. Costa Rica sits around lng -86 to -82,
                 lat 8 to 11, so the FIRST number should be negative.
  addedBy        do not send it. The server sets it from your session, and strips it from
                 update payloads so a request cannot rewrite who added a spot.

Everything else (trailLengthKm, waterfallHeightM, maxOccupancy, permitRequired...) is
optional and only applies to some kinds of spot.

Success: 201 Created
Errors:  401 signed out
         403 signed in but not an admin
         400 validation - the response carries a 'details' object naming each bad field

exec: pm.test("no 'author' field - spots are not user-owned", () =>
console.log("403 - you are signed in but not an admin. Read this request's description.");

request.description:
Edits a spot. ADMIN ONLY.

BODY: send only the fields you want to change - it is a partial update, untouched fields
keep their values.

The route loads the document and calls save(), rather than findByIdAndUpdate, so ALL schema
validators run against the WHOLE document. An invalid enum is rejected even if it sits in a
field you did not send.

Success: 200 OK - returns the updated spot
Errors:  401, 403, 404, or 400 validation

Removes a spot. ADMIN ONLY.

NO BODY.

CASCADES: the post('findOneAndDelete') hook in models/spot.js also deletes every SpotEntry
(someone's toVisit/visited record) and every Review pointing at this spot, so nothing is
left orphaned in the database.

Success: 204 No Content. The response body is EMPTY - that is correct, not a bug. There is
         nothing meaningful to return about a thing that no longer exists.
Errors:  401, 403, 404

item.name: Error cases (what good failures look like)
item.description:
Not busywork - these are exactly the behaviours Parts 1 and 1.5 were built to get right.
Run them to see the difference between 401 and 403, and to see validation errors that name
the field that actually failed.

request.description:
SETUP: run 'Auth > 4. Logout' first.

Shows that the API distinguishes 'I do not know who you are' (401) from 'I know you and you
may not do this' (403). The client needs that difference: 401 means show a login screen,
403 means show an error.

SETUP: run Register, or Login as an account whose role is still 'user'.

This is the entire point of the Part 1 correction. Users explore, visit, vote and review
spots - they do not create them, because a user-submitted spot cannot be verified as a real
and reachable place.

SETUP: must be signed in AS AN ADMIN, otherwise you get 403 before validation ever runs.

Two bad enum values at once. The response names BOTH in a 'details' object keyed by field,
which is the shape react-hook-form wants so it can attach each message to the right input.

This used to return 500. Fixed in Part 1.5 (utils/normalizeError.js).

A string that is not a valid ObjectId. Mongoose throws a CastError, which used to fall
through as a 500. Now correctly 400 - the request was bad, the server was fine.

A perfectly valid ObjectId that matches no document. Contrast with the request above:
malformed id = 400, well-formed id that finds nothing = 404.

SETUP: run '1. Register' first so the email exists.

Returns a clean 'That email is already taken'. It deliberately no longer echoes the raw
MongoDB error, which used to leak the database name, collection name and index name straight
to the client. Fixed in Part 1.5.
